ysabel: hi all, i'm ysabel (first day!) trying to follow the runtime build from source guide but the link stage fails. i'm on Ubuntu 20.04, gcc 11, cuda-11.8 installed via apt. any quick checks? who should i loop in for infra setup? :wave:
paige: welcome :) ping eng-runtime — can you paste the linker error and `nvcc --version`? also check the devex onboarding doc for VM steps.
ysabel: nvcc --version: "Cuda compilation tools, release 11.8, V11.8.89". link error (cmake/ninja):
```
[ 87%] Linking CXX executable bin/runtime_local
/usr/bin/ld: build/_deps/libcuda/lib/libcudnn_static.a(cudnn.o): undefined reference to `cudnnCreate'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
ninja: build stopped: subcommand failed.
```
omar: hmm libcudnn_static showing up in that path is suspicious. run `nvidia-smi` to check driver and `ldd bin/runtime_local` to see library resolution. also make sure CMake found the cuDNN package you intended.
ysabel: nvidia-smi reports "Driver Version: 470.141" (old-ish). ldd shows: `libcudnn.so.8 => not found`, `libcudart.so.11 => /usr/local/cuda-11.8/lib64/libcudart.so.11`.
devon: two possibilities: 1) you didn't install cuDNN system package so the linker picks up a static archive from the submodule path which needs symbols from a different version; 2) driver vs toolkit mismatch (driver 470 might not support newer toolkit features). For dev VMs we recommend the full runfile install of CUDA+cuDNN or the distro packages pinned to the same major versions.
ysabel: i installed libcudnn using apt (`sudo apt install libcudnn8=8.2.1*`) but still see missing at link.
omar: check where apt put it: `dpkg -L libcudnn8 | grep lib` and then add that directory to LD_LIBRARY_PATH or run `sudo ldconfig`. if you're linking against static .a in build/_deps that's probably from an old submodule; try cleaning the build dir `git clean -fdx` (careful) or remove the submodule lib path.
build-bot: reminder: CI uses cuda 11.8 + cudnn 8.2.1 on ubuntu-20.04 images.
ysabel: did `sudo ldconfig` after installing libcudnn8 and set `export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH`. removed build dir and reconfigured cmake. re-ran ninja and the link completed. tests start running locally now. yay :tada:
paige: awesome, glad you got unstuck. devon/omar, can we add a short note to the onboarding doc about prefered cuDNN package names and the driver minimums for ubuntu-20.04 images?
devon: on it 4cc i'll add a checklist: driver >= 510 for CUDA11.8, install `libcudnn8` matching toolkit, run ldconfig, avoid mixing runfile with apt unless you know package splits.
omar: also happy to pair for 30min if you want to run through perf smoke tests and local dev workflow.
ysabel: would love that, thanks everyone. excited to be here :smile:
